paths.description: Homepage and first-load marketplace entry, including preference emulation and promotional overlay.
Solar Panels listing as the representative category/results template, including filters, products, metadata, accessibility, performance, mobile layout, and repeated filter toggling.
Primary product-search journey for “solar panels”; returned CAPTCHA interception.
Representative product-detail path discovered from the category; returned CAPTCHA interception.
Representative verified-manufacturer discovery path; returned CAPTCHA interception.
Public sign-in/account entry to inspect authentication options and permission timing.

findings.summary: A promotional trial interstitial obscures the homepage on arrival.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots after a 5 second wait show a large Accio Work trial modal dimming and blocking the primary Alibaba marketplace content.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not show the promotion on first load. Use an inline, user-invoked promotion or a lightweight dismissible popover after demonstrated intent.

findings.summary: The load-time overlay is not exposed through a native modal primitive in the captured DOM.
findings.evidence: The homepage DOM snapshot taken while the overlay was visible contained no <dialog> or popover element, while the screenshot shows modal behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the flow with <dialog>, showModal(), an accessible name, focus containment, Escape handling, and a clear close button.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-color-scheme: dark, the screenshot remains light and the probe reports colorScheme "normal" with a white body background.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and provide preference-driven surface, text, border, and image treatments using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Long-running decorative motion continues under reduced motion.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe found five running shape-flow animations, each with a 20,000 ms duration, while prefers-reduced-motion: reduce matched.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential looping motion in a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce query and retain only necessary state feedback.

findings.summary: Page and state changes do not use declarative View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The platform-feature CSS probe found no view-transition rules across the representative category interface.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document View Transitions for filter/list state changes and cross-document transitions only where they improve orientation; honor reduced motion.

findings.summary: The long catalog lacks scroll-state-aware navigation cues.
findings.evidence: The 4,991 px category page screenshot and CSS probe show a static desktop header with no scroll-state or scroll progress treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a restrained sticky header or scroll-state query to preserve search/context without consuming excessive space.

findings.summary: Dense persistent filters and navigation crowd the product content.
findings.evidence: At 360 px the fixed desktop filter rail occupies most of the visible width, leaving only a clipped product column.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize products on narrow screens and move secondary filters into an explicit, dismissible filter sheet.

findings.summary: The category template renders a 1,200 px desktop layout on a 360 px viewport.
findings.evidence: Layout evidence reports scrollWidth 1200, clientWidth 360, and 840 px horizontal overflow; the screenshot shows clipped header, breadcrumb, filters, and products.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace fixed/minimum desktop widths with intrinsic grids, fluid sizing, and a mobile filter pattern; verify no overflow at 320–400 px.

findings.summary: Catalog components do not adapt to their available container.
findings.evidence: The category’s filter/product composition remains desktop-sized at 360 px, and the platform CSS probe found no container-query rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the product grid and filter controls container-responsive with @container, intrinsic columns, and a no-query fallback.

findings.summary: Many controls are too small and several links have no visible focus indicator.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 35 target-size failures; the focus probe found many anchors with outline-style none and no box shadow.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 24 by 24 CSS px targets with spacing, retain a strong :focus-visible indicator, and avoid hover-only actions.

findings.summary: Search, manufacturer, and product-detail navigation can dead-end at an anti-bot challenge.
findings.evidence: Fresh search, manufacturer, and product-detail captures all returned “Captcha Interception” and a slide-to-verify challenge instead of results or product content.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce false-positive bot interception, preserve the intended destination, and offer an accessible verification and recovery route.

findings.summary: The traffic challenge provides weak recovery and no path back to the intended task.
findings.evidence: The challenge shows only a slider, QR code, and “Click to feedback”; it does not explain how to resume the search or preserve the query.
findings.suggestedFix: Explain the state, retain the query/destination, provide accessible verification alternatives, retry, and return-to-results actions.

findings.summary: Homepage LCP is slow despite the category template performing well.
findings.evidence: The raw trace measured homepage LCP at 5,256.64 ms. Category Lighthouse measured 2.1 s, showing a template-specific regression.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the real homepage LCP resource, remove the load-time interstitial from the critical path, and defer non-critical bundles.

findings.summary: The homepage ships a very large request graph.
findings.evidence: HAR evidence records 465 requests and 7,776,049 transferred bytes, including 102 scripts (3.60 MB), 222 images (1.61 MB), and multiple parser-inserted stylesheets.
findings.suggestedFix: Set route-level budgets, consolidate critical CSS, lazy-load messenger/RFQ modules, and defer resources until user intent.

findings.summary: Non-critical and partly unused JavaScript is shipped up front.
findings.evidence: The HAR shows large messenger/RFQ bundles on homepage load; Lighthouse found 44 KiB unused in one category bundle (72.7% of that resource).
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by route and interaction, load messaging/RFQ only on demand, and remove legacy/duplicate bundles.

findings.summary: Important controls and links lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed button-name and link-name; the DOM probe counted 114 empty links and 78 images without an alt attribute on the category page.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every interactive element a programmatic name, use real buttons/links, and provide meaningful alt text or empty alt for decoration.

findings.summary: The category page has no main landmark and focus styling is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed landmark-one-main; focus sampling found many anchors with no outline or focus shadow.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap primary content in <main>, normalize heading/landmark structure, and add a clearly visible :focus-visible treatment.

findings.summary: The interface fails narrow reflow and target-size requirements.
findings.evidence: At 360 px the category overflows by 840 px and Lighthouse reports 35 undersized or crowded targets.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow reflow without two-dimensional scrolling and increase target size/spacing while preserving user zoom.

findings.summary: A category JavaScript exception is logged.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading “2”) in cdn-seo-ai-category-wap/index.js.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix the null-state assumption, add guarded parsing, and cover the category payload with regression tests.

findings.summary: Image delivery lacks basic sizing and responsive hints in the observed homepage overlay.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found all three visible images without width/height, two without srcset, and one 600 px image displayed at 134 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic dimensions, provide responsive srcset/sizes, and serve appropriately sized modern formats.

findings.summary: Deprecated unload behavior prevents BFCache restoration.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports an unload listener and four BFCache failure reasons, plus a deprecated API warning.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unload handlers in favor of pagehide/visibilitychange where needed and eliminate actionable no-store/BFCache blockers.

findings.summary: The category has social metadata but no structured entity data.
findings.evidence: Metadata evidence shows complete Open Graph tags but no JSON-LD for the product-list/category entity.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org ItemList/BreadcrumbList metadata that matches the visible products and breadcrumb.

findings.summary: Baseline security headers and cookie protections are missing.
findings.evidence: The HTTPS response has no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy; two 180-day cookies are not Secure and use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy; mark HTTPS cookies Secure and choose the strictest viable SameSite value.

findings.summary: Nearly the entire homepage transfer is attributed to cross-origin infrastructure and telemetry-heavy dependencies.
findings.evidence: HAR reports 461 of 465 requests and 7.74 of 7.78 MB as third-party by origin, while tracker evidence enumerates 12 third-party origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit every cross-origin dependency, treat owned CDNs separately in reporting, remove non-essential telemetry, and defer optional third-party modules until consent or intent.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defense policies are absent.
findings.evidence: Header evidence confirms no CSP/frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options, HSTS, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Add defense-in-depth headers, start CSP in report-only mode, and tighten it using observed violations before enforcement.

findings.summary: Only about half of rendered catalog vocabulary is available in raw HTML.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured 44% homepage and 47% category content coverage without JavaScript. The pages are not empty shells, but substantial product/content detail depends on client rendering.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render or progressively enhance the primary product list, navigation, and task controls so core sourcing remains usable without JavaScript.

findings.summary: Image assets are not consistently right-sized or responsive.
findings.evidence: Image evidence found an oversized 600 px PNG displayed at 134 px and missing responsive sources; the homepage transferred 1.61 MB across 222 images.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate responsive modern-format variants, declare sizes/srcset, and request only the resolution needed for each card or promotion.

findings.summary: Large messaging and RFQ modules load before user intent.
findings.evidence: The homepage HAR includes 600 KB messenger, 554 KB chat, and 465 KB RFQ bundles during initial load.
findings.suggestedFix: Load chat, messenger, RFQ, and related analytics only after the user invokes those features.

findings.summary: The initial page budget is disproportionate to the marketplace landing task.
findings.evidence: The homepage transfers 7.78 MB across 465 requests, with 7.74 MB attributed to origins outside www.alibaba.com.
findings.suggestedFix: Establish a landing-page resource budget and reduce scripts, imagery, telemetry, and cross-origin dependencies before adding new payload.

findings.summary: The marketplace exposes no structured agent tools despite an explicit AI-oriented sourcing surface.
findings.evidence: The homepage advertises “AI Mode”, but the platform probe found no WebMCP/agent tool registration; Lighthouse agentic-browsing scored 0.33.
findings.suggestedFix: Pilot narrowly scoped, permissioned WebMCP tools for product search, comparison, and RFQ drafting with clear confirmation boundaries.

taskList.title: Rebuild category mobile reflow and input targets
Remove the first-load interstitial and use a semantic, user-invoked dialog
Add baseline security headers and secure cookie attributes
Reduce homepage payload and defer chat, RFQ, and telemetry
Fix accessible names, landmarks, focus, and target sizing
Reduce anti-bot false positives and preserve task recovery
Right-size responsive images and reserve their layout space
Fix console errors, deprecated unload handling, and BFCache blockers
Add category structured data and pilot safe agent tools
Add restrained transition and scroll orientation cues
